rationale: The conditioning spread is character-for-character identical to the archived DebtGoodwillGrossProfitGap (rising goodwill minus rising gross profit) with only the financing gate swapped from debt issuance to cash drawdown, making this a cosmetic re-gating of an already-tested signal rather than a new mechanism.

This is the archived ShortDebtIntangibleCollateralMismatch with levels swapped for trends/deltas and the expected sign flipped to match the already-observed +3.9 t-stat, i.e., a post-hoc sign reversal on a near-duplicate expression rather than an independent test.

Economically coherent and distinct from the archived capex-mix signals, but note the mechanical redundancy that falling PP&E simultaneously raises GP/PP&E and lowers PP&E growth, so the spread partly double-counts asset shrinkage rather than cleanly contrasting productivity with expansion.

This is essentially a linear repackaging of two well-documented published anomalies (acquirer/investment underperformance and the R&D-intensity premium), with the two shares mechanically anti-correlated inside a common budget so the subtraction adds little beyond a standard composite.

This is the sign-mirrored, levels-to-changes restatement of the archived InventoryBuildPhysicalKnowledgeGap (inventory build conditioned on knowledge versus physical capital), so it tests the same economics already shown to work at t=-3.05 rather than a substantively new one.

The R&D-versus-capex/acquisition use-of-proceeds contrast is a defensible and reasonably distinct refinement of the archived ExternalFinancePhysicalTilt, though the pure-rank issuance gate means the sign is driven almost entirely by the mix spread and the incremental content over the known net-issuance anomaly needs to be demonstrated.
